chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabiy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the daughter of the brother due to breastfeeding: I do not command anyone [to marry her] nor do I prohibit it, but I only prohibit it for myself and my sons.

And it was said: The daughter of Hamzah was proposed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for marriage, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) refused and said: 'She is the daughter of my brother due to breastfeeding.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.ابْنَةَ حَمْزَةَ: Daughter of Hamzah (referring to Zaynab bint Jahsh)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on marrying a milk-brother's daughter?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the status of *milk kinship* (radāʿ) by distinguishing between a general prohibition and a personal preference (istihbāb) for the Ahl al-Bayt, as Ali (AS) declared it permissible for the general public but prohibited it for himself and his descendants. It references the Prophet’s refusal to marry Zaynab bint Jahsh, though Shia scholars often contextualize this within the broader narrative of the marriage to establish the permanence of milk kinship ties. The ruling underscores the principle that milk relationships create the same marital barriers as blood relationships, a concept deeply rooted in early Islamic jurisprudence.
